title: Conductor Cloud persistent workspaces for coding-agent teams
summary: Conductor introduced persistent cloud workspaces built on isolated microVMs, with share links, multiplayer access, and an API for agent-driven development environments.
why_it_matters: Infrastructure teams are moving some coding-agent execution from laptop worktrees to persistent shared environments, shifting isolation, identity, audit, secret, network, and cost controls into the platform evaluation.
caveats: A vendor launch is a signal to evaluate, not evidence that the service meets an organization's security or reliability requirements.
Persistent workspaces expand the lifecycle of source code, credentials, logs, and network access beyond a laptop session.
Pricing, regional availability, enterprise controls, data handling, and deletion guarantees need first-hand validation before adoption.
adoption_question: Can the platform demonstrate least-privilege identity, secret isolation, egress policy, auditability, retention controls, incident response, and bounded per-workspace cost?
example_reason: This is an evaluation checklist for an external platform; a local infrastructure stub would not test its security or operational properties.
